LEGO Speed Champions Lamborghini Urus ST-X and Lamborghini Huracán Super Trofeo EVO 76899 Building Kit (663 Pieces) I built this kit with my very LEGO-experienced 6-year-old, who found it to be just a little too challenging for her to do on her own (note that the box says 8+, but she has put together many 8+ kits on her own). Overall, I found this to be a fun little kit to put together, even though I'm not exactly a car guy. One of the models looks like a traditional black Lamborghini, while the other looks almost like an SUV in comparison, but it's probably jus the scale and the boxiness of the LEGO kits that makes me think this. In addition, you get a starting line that shifts left and right to give you green or red lights, which is a nice little added benefi.

The ads for this one talk about racing the cars, but it's all imaginary - there's no pull-back action or anything like you can get in Tecnic models - and the two included minifigs are basic to the point of being disappointing. Most of the pieces in this one are very small, and there's not much movement in the final models at all. Many of the other bigger pieces have decals, so there's limited use in terms of using this to build other models.

If you have a little car fan at home, this will thrill them. We're not car people, so we thought it was only just a bit better than OK.

text_fidelity_a:
LEGO DUPLO Town Steam Train 10874 Remote Control Set - Learning Toy and Daycare Accessory for Toddlers, Boys, Girls, and Kids 2-5 Years Old, Push and Go Battery Powered Set with RC Function I really love these Duplo Lego sets. While I do not have any little ones in the house, I like having some toys on hand for the occasional visitors with kids. These are always a hit and now when friends with little ones come over, the kids always remember our place because of the "Lego Lady!" haha! Bringing out the Legos has brought shy little ones out of their shell as they put together the pieces and play away.

This train set is great! it is super simple to put together, as with any Duplo set. You will need to unscrew the battery box to put in 4 AAA batteries, though. If you're lazy like me and don't want to trudge out to the garage for a screwdriver, you can easily open it with a table knife (haha.. see pic). To make the train go, first be sure there are batteries installed and then push the on/off button on the bottom. put the train on the track. The wheels straddle the inner upright portions of the track (see pic). Then simply give the train a little push and off it goes around the track.

To control the train, use the little action tiles. These are flat pieces with a small icon on them. There is one for each of the following actions. When the train goes over it, it performs the action:
- whistle (yellow) makes a train whistle sound
- horn (white) makes one toot sound - I thought this was for the lights but those didnt come on when it went over this one
- water (blue) stops for a bit there and makes a sound like it is getting water for the steam engine
- reverse (green) stops and reverses the train
- stop (red) stops the train

The action bricks are really easy to put down on the track - they just lay in the middle of the track and don't actually attach. So it is easy for the little ones to pick them up and move them around. This is super fun for the kiddos and definitely keeps them happy occupied for quite some time!

There is an App you can get as well - works for iPhone, iPad, and Android devices. It has nothing to do with the train set itself, though. I thought maybe it did, but it is really just a separate app/Game. It is a fun little game for young kids, though. App Tip: if you have an iPhone and aren't getting any sound with the app, be sure you don't have the device on mute. (for iPhones it is that side button you switch on/off). I don't have an iPad but I suspect it could have the same issue.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO DUPLO Town Steam Train 10874 Remote Control Set - Learning Toy and Daycare Accessory for Toddlers, Boys, Girls, and Kids 2-5 Years Old, Push and Go Battery Powered Set with RC Function

You can use the pieces inside to create very simple roll-and-move style games, but nothing that even comes close to any level of complexity that a modern board game design (even those by Haba, or those designed specifically for young children) might contain. Picking up the ball,  placing it in the hole, and pushing it through is what we have been working on and he is getting the hang of it. Pulling the lever will be what we work on next. He isn't walking yet, but big sister is, and she loves pulling it around by the string. She puts her little princess figurines in it pretending they drive the truck, so it's sparking some imaginative play. Overall, I think it's a great toy that will grow with him!

text_fidelity_a: The ONE Music Group Hi-Lite, 88 Keys LED Light Bar, Smart Device for Piano Learning Beginners (TOH1) First off, I have a Casio 61-key lighted keyboard which is way cool to learn a song with, but of course, it is NOT a full-sized keyboard.  I also have a Roland FA-08 88-keyboard workstation and I LOVE playing on it, but learning a new song, I would like the same ability on the Roland as I have on the Casio.  Along comes this neat keyboard LED bar that is similar to the Casio's lighted keys and I think yeah!  Not so fast...first, the software for this item is ONLY available for Android devices.  I guess I'm a bit different...I have a Kindle which won't download it since Kindle has it's own OS.  I have a small Acer tablet/computer but it runs on Windows...I have two 15.5 inch screen computers - one running the Chrome OS, the other Windows.  So...my only Android device is my phone.  A tiny little thing to connect to this app and be able to see the keys while playing...I have tried some workarounds to no avail and am just not all that impressed since the people who created it didn't think that they should make this available across more than just Android devices...jeez!

I almost thought the grill was big enough to be one of those lap desk sizes, and I feel you could definitely use it as such for smaller kids, but it’s also fine on a tabletop too. The grill top portion could be a little nicer. I realize the paper piece allows the grill image to be present, so I think that’s great for the flame details, but an actual plastic grate on top of the image would be much more interesting and realistic. The drizzle is a new item that we haven’t tried before, and I’m honestly not into this liquidy element—it’s just one of those things to get on clothes and make a mess. text_fidelity_a:
Thames and Kosmos Remote-Control Machines DLX My nearly 12 year old daughter was super thrilled to see this box sitting on the counter when she got home from school. She immediately tore into it and with mom (me) helping her for awhile she began to build the robotic arm. I eventually bowed out since she was obviously fine building it without parental supervision. I was amazed at all the various parts. 3 motors, a remote control and lots of plastic parts that somehow come together into various machine creations. She had the robotic arm completely built that evening and it was picking up things like doggie toys, socks and iPods then rotating around and releasing them into a box. The robotic arm tended to want to fall over when it raised up too high but she figured out how to build onto the base to stabilize it.

The instruction booklet is very detailed, but it only has pictures. the pictures are full color and you must carefully study it a bit to understand what connectors you need to what parts, and exactly how they're connected together. She said she would have liked a few written instruction but the pictures were fine. So it would seem that no particular language is required to build the various machines in the box. The pictures are not simple and they take some time to study, but they are very well done. She also said it's a great set and she will be disassembling the robotic arm to build other ideas given in the book. After a few are built, I expect her to come up with some original designs of her own. I think the book is superb at showing how to build and should plant seeds to stimulate an interested person into building some of their own creations.

The parts included will only build what is given in the book. If you or your child want to build even more exotic machines, then a second kit might need to be purchased. I think this is a great starter kit to get someone interested in building machines/robots but it is limited by the amount of parts included. And it doesn't include batteries. She used 5 AA batteries to get her robotic arm to work. But it was pretty cool watching her manipulate it via remote control. I personally feel girls should be given such gifts and encouraged to build these things. It is superb in helping them understand how things work in relation to each other. My daughter told me she understood how it functioned and even took the time to describe to me in detail how this part turns this part which causes this part to do this and so on.... I was extremely pleased.
text_fidelity_b: Thames and Kosmos Remote-Control Machines DLX

Boom Boom Balloon, Exciting Anticipation Family Board Game Outdoor Summer Toy, for Kids Ages 8 and up My oldest son(5) recently started daily injections. As you would expect, he hates them. We try to do something fun after each of them, and this was used as one of his "surprises". It did the trick and took his mind off that mean needle.

This game is really fun! Not only did my children enjoy it, but I did, too. It does come with a few issues, though.

First of all, as I put the thing together, the instructions say to never use your mouth to blow up the balloon. You must use a balloon pump. A balloon pump isn't included, so I chose to use my mouth to blow up the balloon, since I had excited children waiting to play. It went fine. I was able to blow up the balloon while it was in the frame without any problem.

Secondly, we couldn't get the top clip piece to stay put. There's a clip that holds the 3 pieces of the frame together at the top. It kept coming lose no matter how tight I tried to get it. When I took the thing apart, I couldn't get one frame piece to come apart. So, 2 were so lose the whole thing kept coming apart, but one was so tight I had to put it in the box together, and therefore, couldn't close the lid.

Third, one of the sticks was broke within minutes of playing the game. Thankfully, there are 4 extras included, so we can still play. Plus, the recommended age is 8 and up. I played this game with my 2 and 5 year olds. The 2 year old is the one that broke the stick, so I'm not taking stars off for that issue or anything. It's simply to warn you that they do break pretty easily.

There are 12 balloons included. They are all the same: blue, with a face. They are the regular sized balloons, so I imagine this game will work perfectly fine with store bought replacement balloons. You just probably won't have a face on there.

I know it sounds like a lot of complaining up there, but we really enjoyed this game!

The basics: You put the thing together, which is really simple. You put the balloon in the frame, blow it up, and then wrap it around the "hook" at the bottom to keep the air in without having to actually tie it. Super simple. You take the sticks and put them in the holes(6) until you hear the first click. Then you take turns rolling dice. Whatever number it lands on is the amount of times you push in a stick. It can be the same stick or one click each on different sticks. Whoever pops the balloon first loses(or wins if you're my children).

Overall, it's a fun game that's worth the issues that come with it.
text_fidelity_b: Boom Boom Balloon, Exciting Anticipation Family Board Game Outdoor Summer Toy, for Kids Ages 8 and up

text_fidelity_a:
Marvel Guardians of The Galaxy Big Blastin' Rocket Raccoon Figure, 10 Inch I'm going to review this not from the perspective of a toy, but rather as a piece of movie memorabilia. Years ago, I use to love to go to the local mall here in Austin and stop by the SunCoast Motion Picture Company store. Where you could buy all sort of movie related items as well as the movies themselves. Over the years I've bought a number of items very similar to this Rocket Raccoon figure for my collection. So when I was offered one of these 10 inch figure to check out I gladly accepted.

I wasn't expecting this figure to be so big - I knew it was suppose to be 10" but it seems bigger than that to me. It came in one of those open face boxes that allow you to actually touch the toy before taking it out of the box, and you can activate the sound effect as the item ships with the batteries already installed and the sound box is set in a demo mode. The sounds it make are pretty loud, they should put a smile on any child face (and a frown on any adults in the room).

Once out of the box, there is some assembly required. You have to pop the tail into the figures rear-end (yeah, I know). It takes some effort to do that, so I suggest having an adult do it. Other than that, the figure is ready to go. Like I mentioned there is a demo mode on the effects box. The effects are controlled with a three-position switch - Off, Try Me (demo), and On. The unit is powered by three double-A batteries which are located in the figures backpack (there is a screw securing the cover to the batteries). Once you turn on the power switch, there are two activation points - one on the figures leg and another on top of the gun he is holding. Pressing one or the other activates both motion and sound effects, plus the figure speaks phrases from the movie. The motion effects are just the end of the gun rotating and the figure shaking a bit. There are some light effects with the end of the gun & gun sight lighting up. There aren't that many spoken phrases - so they can get a bit repetitive after awhile.

The toy is pretty well made - a lot more substantial than most of the movie memorabilia, but then again it was made for kids to play with.

I kept the figure on my desk at work for about a week before bringing it home. I can't tell you how times people stopped and played with the figure (too many times, as that is what prompted me to finally take it home). I haven't seen the movie yet - but it is definitely one that I plan on seeing this summer.

I really like this figure - about the only thing I could comment on would be the detail of the end of his gun, everything else has a decent level of detail, but that part of the gun doesn't. Guessing that is more due to the fact that they made it out of clear plastic so that the light effect could be seen.
text_fidelity_b: Marvel Guardians of The Galaxy Big Blastin' Rocket Raccoon Figure, 10 Inch

Fisher-Price Connect Digital Soother We are using this soother with an 8 month old who generally sleeps very well.

Pros - Easy to use and the sounds, volume control, and lighting are well done.

Cons- Expensive, goes through batteries fast, not that interesting to our baby. He watches it for a short time and then loses interest (just as well if you are putting him to sleep). The biggest problem is that our machine goes to sleep after a short while and then won't restart.

Nothing compares to the old Fisher-Price Rainforest soother from 10 years ago that had water in it. My first grandson loved it and it lasted for years.

I agree with an earlier reviewer that the Cloud B Sleep Sheep is a better buy for providing the soft white noise that both soothes your baby and masks other sounds in the house. All five of my grand kids have some kind of sound machine in their bedroom, ranging from the $26 sheep to a $100 Ecotones Sound + Sleep Machine (I've bought five of those for adult family members).

I also think the kids go to sleep quicker and sleep more soundly in a totally dark room with no visual stimulation.
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Connect Digital Soother

text_fidelity_a:
QOGELY Home Decor Blaster Building Kits This is not a “puzzle”, but a “model”. I can only assume that they do not have a word for “model” in Chinese. Because Chinese companies always list items like this is a “puzzle” though it’s really not.

This model is made of wood. It shows to have 47 pieces. There are 3 boards with the cutout pieces. You’ll want to use caution when removing the pieces from the boards so that you do not break them. You remove the pieces from the boards as you go. The pieces are numbered on the instruction sheet, but not on the boards. So if you remove them all at 1st, it will make it very difficult to put the model together. I highly recommend you have either a razor blade or thin sharp knife available to help remove the pieces. If you simply use your fingers, you could easily break a piece.

I must admit that I am not a person who likes to build models. So it took me about an hour and ½ to put this together. It turned out okay, but not as perfect as the pictures. The shingles do not fit perfectly. Nonetheless I think it looks okay.

Also, when you get to pieces 12, 13, 14 and 15 which is part of instruction number 5… Those 4 pieces make a little platform. The way the instruction show it on instruction number 9, that platform sits inside section B. But if you place it there, then the top shingle portion sits on top of the platform and is not sturdy. If you don’t put that platform there, then the top piece see fits in to the bottom piece a which makes it sturdy. Then I use that platform as a base on the bottom to place the temple on top of. Written on that platform is “Temple of Serenity”. So because of that, I think it should go on the bottom is a base anyway. But of course you can do it anyway you want to.

An optional string of LED lights is included. Two AA batteries are required and not included.

As a bonus, there is also a small “Ellie House” which is 24 pieces.

This model is made in China and being sold by a Chinese company on Amazon. At the current price of 30 bucks I think it is a bit expensive, but it is a unique and interesting item. Also, it comes in a nice cardboard box, which makes it easy for wrapping if you’re giving it as a gift.
text_fidelity_b: QOGELY Home Decor Blaster Building Kits

BraveRats - A Game by Seiji Kanai After attempting to play this game, I was confused. Honestly, I went to look around at reviews to see what I was missing. I saw such words as “bluffing” and “strategy” and I was left with, “What?!” It seemed like I had a completely different game. It takes a little time to understand everything, though. Without the cheat sheet close by, it was impossible for me to figure out who won. Even then, the “special powers” confused me. The cheat sheet would tell me the winner of a certain combination, but then according to the “special powers”, the other card should have won. (After reading through the instructions again, I saw that the special powers always override the cheat sheet.) I’m embarrassed about my confusion, but I’m throwing it out there in case I can make anybody else out there that’s confused like me feel better.

There are 8 red cards, 8 blue cards, a cheat sheet, and a booklet, all in a tin case. It’s a very quick game. Though it seems like it would be simple, it can be complicated at first. Once you get the hang of it, it is simple, though.

I imagine this will be a perfect game to play with my little ones when they’re a bit older. (My oldest is a delayed 5 right now, but I imagine slightly older children will have fun with this!)

Really, once the initial confusion is dealt with, this is a fun little game!
text_fidelity_b: BraveRats - A Game by Seiji Kanai

text_fidelity_a:
Escape Room in a Box: Flashback, Escape Room Game with 19 Puzzles and 4 Locks, Can Pair with Amazon Alexa, For Adults and Teens 13 Years Old and Up It's an 80s themed box, with a name like "Flashback" that has nothing to do with the 80s, and very little to do with "flashbacks". It's actually about werewolves, a magic ring, and bad poetry. The story makes no sense at all, and that's the easiest element of an escape room, really. Fortunately, everything else in this box is pretty good.

We played with a group of 4 people, which was perfect. You could even do six and have a great time with it. The game is broken into three paths - red, purple and blue, each with a very vague theme like "poems" (blue), "childhood" (purple) and "dinosaurs" (red) - and you need to complete all three in order to win. We broke our group of four into two teams of two and tackled blue and purple envelopes separately, then worked together on the red and the final puzzle. Each envelope took us roughly the same amount of time to beat, and the final puzzle was appropriately paced to be solved quickly. Most other escape room games we've played, from Unlock to Exit to Escape the Room all suffer from pacing problems, or narrowing you down to having only one puzzle or a few cards to work with at one time, which is nice for pointing out the way to solve some more complex puzzles, but which makes it rather difficult to play with more than two people - this box has solved that problem.

Overall, we were pretty impressed with this with a few caveats. One of the puzzles requires you to do something to the game pieces that is spelled out early on in the letter. It wasn't difficult to figure out what to do, but it was difficult to execute. It's hard to say more without giving out spoilers for one of the "coolest" puzzles in the box, but let's just say that it was mechanically difficult to work with. One of the puzzles at the end of the game required another outside prop that's easy to deal with, but the amount of finagleing with the pieces and the prop left us questioning if we had solved that puzzle correctly (we did, but it wasn't quite clear).

One touch that I particularly liked was how the game color-coded everything according to the paths/envelopes, and how the locked boxes worked - they performed exacly as they should have, and they were high enough quality that we felt like we could toss them around a little without any issues.

This is expensive for a one-time-use product, but it's definitely my favorite of the escape room games for a medium to large sized group, and it's probably pretty good for two slueths to solve on their own as well.

Solved in 1:07:11.
text_fidelity_b: Escape Room in a Box: Flashback, Escape Room Game with 19 Puzzles and 4 Locks, Can Pair with Amazon Alexa, For Adults and Teens 13 Years Old and Up

text_fidelity_a:
Lorsaberus Light Saber, 10 Mode Sound RGB 12 Color Changeable Metal Hilt Light Sabers, Dueling Smooth Swing Light Saber Sword Toy for Men,Children's Day Gifts (1 inch Blade)-Grey [[VIDEOID:3325afb06624e7eb67d7487ba5918892]] This is a well made little product. When I use the word "little" I mean it literally in the sense that it is much smaller than a Star Wars™ light-saber that they use for props in the movies. Although I do have big hands . . . unless Alec Guinness and Mark Hamill have teensy-tiny hands, this is about an inch smaller than the ones they used to battle the empire.

The diameter is just a little bigger than a US Quarter coin and just over 1 inch. The ones in the movie are closer to over 2 inches by my estimation.

All that being said, this is still a fun little toy light-saber, if a little overpriced in my opinion. At the current price of $120, I'd say wait for a sale.

It is well made and the colors and sounds are well done. It has motion-sensing so the sounds will change when you "swing" it at a stormtrooper, for instance. (see video).

There are quite a few different modes that can be set by double-clicking on the power button once it's turned on.

It is very LOUD as well, so be aware. There is no volume control for the sound that I can tell -- nothing in the instructions about it. The instructions are just a 1-page printout, but they're fairly thorough, so I can't complain. The translation is not that bad -- average, but understandable-ish.

It recharges quickly and it can go at least an hour without the battery dying. I haven't messed with it enough to see exactly how long the battery will last, but it recharges pretty quickly.

The "saber" portion is just a piece of semi-opaque PVC tubing with a curved "nose-cone" on the end to give it a rounded look. It looks decent. It's covered in protective film that you can peel off for a nice look. I didn't peel it off all the way yet because I'm thinking of maybe mounting it on a wall mounted display box to nerd-out my office more.

This would be fun for a child/adult who's into anything Star Wars™ but I don't think it's an "officially" licensed Lucasfilm product. Does it matter? It doesn't actually claim to be anywhere on the box or labeling that I can see and I'm not sure that the term "light saber" is trademarked or copyrighted, so unless you care to have the "official".

If you are considering this for a child, be aware -- it's not sharp, but the "saber" part is not a soft piece of plastic. By that I mean . . . if you get hit with a good swing, it's going to leave a mark. Not as bad as getting hit with a Louisville Slugger™ . . . but still . . . probably not a good gift idea for the younger kiddos.

Overall, it's a neat product, but I had to take off a star because it's smaller than the movie version and the price is quite steep for a toy, even considering that it's a very nice quality toy.

And did I mention very fun? Now I must go and take care of that annoying Vader guy.
text_fidelity_b: Lorsaberus Light Saber, 10 Mode Sound RGB 12 Color Changeable Metal Hilt Light Sabers, Dueling Smooth Swing Light Saber Sword Toy for Men,Children's Day Gifts (1 inch Blade)-Grey

text_fidelity_a:
Thames & Kosmos Drop It | Super Fun Family Strategy Game | Parents' Choice Silver Award Winner, Multi-Color Drop It is a simple game - you drop shapes into a Plinko-like contraption,, and depending on what happens when they fall, you earn points, so long as you follow some simple placement rules - you cannot touch the same shapes or colors, and the edges have restrictions on what shapes can touch them. It's so simple, and yet it's incredibly fun.

Not only is this a fun game though, it's a game that really teaches young players how to formulate an argument, identify problems with shape placement, and think about how and what to play. I played with a five-year-old who has no strategic ability yet, but who was able to, after just one play, identify if a shape was correctly placed right away and push forward with better strategy in her second game. The older child was better able to adapt, but also showed great ability to arrange and save her shapes for times when they'd be advantageous for use.

My one concern with this game is that it is quite a bit more difficult with three players, since that is the player count in which only three of the four colors are in use, and it's harder to place pieces. This is easily remedied by a simple rules change.

This is one of the best kids games I've ever played, and far and away one of the best games I've played recently. Get it.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Drop It | Super Fun Family Strategy Game | Parents' Choice Silver Award Winner, Multi-Color

LEGO Star Wars Death Star (10188) (Discontinued by manufacturer) From the pictures, this looked kind of goofy at first. I really wanted the other Death Star, but that's much harder to find than this one. This one is still super rare, and I didn't fall in love with it until we put it together. It has so many cool scenes from the movies, and so many working parts. It even has a removable tie fighter, with a tie fighter hanger. It's got a ton of cool figures that I haven't seen anywhere else, like R2-D2, Assassin Droid, R2-Q5, Protocol Droid, Interrogation Droid, Palpatine, Darth Vader, Imperial Trooper, Luke Skywalker (Jedi, Stormtrooper, and Tatooine), Obi Wan Kenobi, Han Solo (Stormtrooper and Black Vest), Stormtrooper, Princess Leia, C-3PO, Grand Moff Tarkin, Mouse Guard, Royal Guard, and Chewie.

It took four of us two full days to put this together, over Christmas holidays, but it was well worth the effort. The scale is a little strange, but it's that way in almost any lego set. We calculated that if they made a Lego Death Star to the scale where people would actually make sense, then it would have to be 2 miles across. So, they had to make some design choices so that a lot of stuff isn't really to scale. For reference, the real Death Star is 100 miles across. This set does mix up different scenes from two different movies. But, they're really cool scenes. A lot of the parts work, like you can crush Luke and Leia in the trash compactor and you can move and aim the Death Star ray on two different axes.

The instruction book is ginormous. There are about 500 different steps in total. It's spiral bound, and you have to be really careful so that it doesn't rip. Overall, this is an epic set, and I highly recommend this to anyone who's an expert with Legos.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Star Wars Death Star (10188) (Discontinued by manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Ravensburger Harbor in Portofino, Italy 1000 Piece Puzzle I cannot help but parrot the reviews I've done for my other two Ravensburger puzzles because each one has impressed me the same, and got me somewhat addicted to puzzles (something I used to love as a kid, in smaller form):

Basically, I originally thought Ravensburger's claim to "outstanding quality" sounded ridiculous - it's a puzzle right? But it really is outstanding quality. The pieces are crisp and you barely ever get a false positive. Meanwhile, there is very little dust and paper shavings in the box compared to other puzzles I've done.

As for this puzzle in particular, it's a beautiful picture that has lots of similar shades of colors, making for an excellent challenge, without being absurdly frustrating.

Arrange to do this on a proper sized backer board so you can move it out of the way; it may take longer than you think.

An excellent puzzle, indeed.
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Harbor in Portofino, Italy 1000 Piece Puzzle

text_fidelity_a:
VTech Baby Lil' Critters Shake and Wobble Busy Ball Amazon Exclusive, Purple This toy is GREAT for entertaining a baby. Due to the language and songs played, I would NOT RECOMMEND this toy for any vegan or anyone who isn't interested in supporting the dairy industry. It's one thing to sing cute songs about happy cows on the farm...but it almost felt cult-like with its lyrics constantly berating your child about how they should drink their milk. I don't love that.

My baby has been entertaining herself with this toy since she was 4 months old. At 6 months, she still likes it a lot. It is used at the dinner table to keep her entertained while we all eat. It almost always works through most of the meal. I highly recommend it as a toy that can distract a child. We don't let her have it outside of mealtime so it keeps it fresh and interesting.

It does have a surprising amount of songs to it. Even several weeks after ownership a few songs were played that we hadn't heard before. But there are some songs that get played all the time. 2 months of ownership and the parents aren't yet annoyed by it so that's a good thing.

I took a star off for the incessant dairy promoting lyrics which just seem strange and I'm convinced that the dairy industry had some involvement in their creation.
text_fidelity_b: VTech Baby Lil' Critters Shake and Wobble Busy Ball Amazon Exclusive, Purple
